## Professional Experience — Overview
Quy holds six roles spanning IT administration, research, retail, and teaching. Current: IT System Administrator II at the University of Toledo (Jan 2026 – Present). Also current: Undergraduate Research Assistant at UToledo (Dec 2025 – Present). Previously held concurrently: IT Support Technician at UToledo (Dec 2025 – May 2026). Prior roles: Sales Associate at Harbor Freight Tools (Mar 2025 – Feb 2026), Summer Camp Tutor at Explorers Academy (Summer 2025), and Sales Advisor at Best Buy (Sep 2024 – Jan 2025).

## IT System Administrator — Level II | University of Toledo (Jan 2026 – Present)
Quy manages 1,000+ Windows and macOS endpoints through **Active Directory** and **Microsoft Intune**, enforcing device compliance policies and triaging security alerts across the fleet. He owns endpoint lifecycle management — imaging, deployment, OS and application patching, and hardware refresh cycles that keep the fleet in compliance — and provides Tier 2 support for 250+ classrooms and offices, resolving desktop, network, printer, and peripheral failures and documenting root cause for the Tier 1 queue.

In his first four months in the role, Quy responded to 15+ security incidents: identifying and remediating unpatched Windows 10 endpoints carrying open vulnerabilities, and isolating 2 malware-infected devices from the network. This role is held concurrently with the IT Support Technician and Undergraduate Research Assistant positions and covers a superset of the Support Technician scope.

## Undergraduate Research Assistant | University of Toledo (Dec 2025 – Present)
Working with the Medical Department, Quy develops Python/OpenCV video tracking and behavior-state analysis to extract zebrafish motion features from Novel Tank Test footage. He prepares labeled trial data and training workflows that estimate compound-family probabilities, evaluate models, and flag novel responses — a cross-disciplinary role bridging computer science with clinical research. Held concurrently with the IT System Administrator role.

## IT Support Technician | University of Toledo (Dec 2025 – May 2026)
Triaged 10-15 tickets per week through UToledoHelp, the university's in-house ticketing platform, spanning same-day fixes to multi-day network and hardware escalations. Escalated each case through a structured process, writing resolution notes clear enough for the next technician to reproduce the fix. Held concurrently with the IT System Administrator and Research Assistant roles.

## Sales Associate | Harbor Freight Tools (March 2025 – Feb 2026)
Maintained email capture above 80% per transaction and membership sign-ups at 1.5%, meeting store growth goals, while keeping extended warranty sales above 11.5% and consistently hitting 90%+ of daily sales budget. Handled data entry and floor work simultaneously in a high-traffic store, adjusting quickly to changing store needs using judgment and problem-solving, and explained technical product details in simple, clear steps customers could easily follow.

## Summer Camp Tutor | Explorers Academy (Summer 2025)
Instructed students in computer science fundamentals, making abstract concepts like algorithms, logical reasoning, and programming tangible through hands-on, real-world workshops. Mentored student-led projects focused on creativity, collaboration, and curiosity in STEM. This role sharpened Quy's ability to communicate technical ideas clearly to non-technical audiences — a skill actively applied when educating university staff on cybersecurity best practices.

## Sales Advisor | Best Buy (Sep 2024 – Jan 2025)
Served as a tech-focused brand ambassador, bridging customer needs with appropriate technology solutions through active listening and deep product knowledge. Maintained continuous learning on new hardware and software to provide accurate, informed recommendations. Cultivated consultative communication skills to quickly build trust with non-technical stakeholders.

## Personal Life

### Background & Identity
Quy was born and raised in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. He came to the US as an international student his freshman year at the University of Toledo, drawn by a 75% scholarship offer, a strong CS program, and relatives already living nearby. By his sophomore year, his entire family had relocated to the US. He is now a permanent resident — no visa sponsorship required under any circumstances.

### Personality
Quy is competitive and driven — he plays to win, in games, academics, and career. He is also outgoing and collaborative, thriving in team environments, and consistently creative and curious, always exploring the intersection of security, AI, and real-world impact.

### Hobbies & Interests

**Sports & Fitness:**
Quy plays basketball, badminton, and pickleball. He stays physically sharp as a counterbalance to long hours at the keyboard.

**Gaming:**
A dedicated PC gamer with a competitive esports background. He played Valorant on the University of Toledo's varsity esports team. His final semester, the team pushed all the way to the semi-finals, falling just one point short — a proud memory of what the team built together. He has since stepped back to focus on growing workloads and personal projects, but the competitive mindset never left.

**Music:**
His taste spans lo-fi / chill beats for deep focus sessions, hip-hop and R&B, and Vietnamese and broader Asian music that keeps him connected to his roots.

**Travel:**
Quy has traveled across Southeast Asia — Singapore, Thailand, and Malaysia — and made the long journey to the United States where he now lives. A global perspective informs how he thinks about technology and security across different cultures and systems.

## Work Preferences & Availability

**Location:** Open to remote, hybrid, or on-site — no preference, fully flexible.
**Availability:**
- Part-time roles: Available now
- Summer internship: Seeking a Summer 2027 cybersecurity internship
- Full-time: Available from December 2027 (graduation)
- No visa sponsorship needed — Permanent Resident

**Preferred Environment:** Startups and fast-paced teams where ownership matters and things move quickly. Quy thrives when he can take initiative, wear multiple hats, and see the direct impact of his work — not waiting in a slow enterprise pipeline.

## Work Philosophy & Mindset

### Problem-Solving Approach
When Quy hits a wall, his first move is independent — he digs into documentation, researches the issue thoroughly, and stress-tests his own assumptions before reaching out. He treats every stuck moment as a learning opportunity, not a blocker. Once he has exhausted his own analysis, he brings the problem to peers or supervisors — not just asking for answers, but sharing his findings and asking for their perspective and recommendations. This approach means he rarely shows up empty-handed, and the solutions he builds stick because he understands them deeply.

### Handling Pressure & Failure
Quy is self-motivated under pressure. When things go wrong — a project stalls, a model underperforms, a competition is lost by one point — his response is to lock in, not spiral. He actively rebuilds momentum by focusing on what he can control: his effort, his preparation, and his attitude. He has learned that resilience is not the absence of setbacks but the speed at which you reset and move forward. That mindset carried him through competitive Valorant, late-night debugging sessions, and live incident response situations.

### What Excites Him Most
Quy is most energized at the intersection of threat hunting and AI tooling — identifying real threats and then building intelligent systems to reduce the manual workload of finding them. He thinks constantly about how AI and cybersecurity can reinforce each other: smarter detection, automated response, adversarial-resistant models. His long-term vision is to build systems that protect people at scale, the same way he wishes something had protected him when he was that kid who lost his Steam account.

## Elevator Pitch (Use this when asked "tell me about Quy" or "who is Quy?" or "give me a summary")
Operator Quy is a Computer Science student at the University of Toledo, graduating December 2027, with a 3.6 GPA. He works at the intersection of cybersecurity and AI — currently serving as an IT System Administrator Level II, managing 1,000+ devices and responding to live security incidents. He is a Cybersecurity Analyst & Developer on Sentra, a team-built AI-powered phishing detection platform, and an Undergraduate Research Assistant building Python/OpenCV video tracking for zebrafish drug-response studies. Originally from Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, he is a permanent US resident seeking a Summer 2027 cybersecurity internship and open to full-time positions from December 2027. His mission: build intelligent systems that protect people at scale.

## Origin Story
Quy's drive to protect digital assets was forged through personal experience. As a young gamer, he fell victim to a phishing attack on Steam — a fake login page disguised as a skin giveaway, made convincing by a fabricated display of active players. He entered his credentials, was bypassed through a fake authentication layer, and lost a paid account he had built up over years. Rather than just a cautionary tale, this became the core motivation behind every security system he builds today: no one else should lose something they worked hard for because of deceptive design.

## Projects — Overview
Quy's flagship project is Sentra, an AI phishing detection platform built with a 4-person team, where he serves as Cybersecurity Analyst & Developer. He also has two personal projects in earlier stages: a Personal Cyber Intelligence Operator (in development) and CyberLab (planned).

## Sentra — AI Phishing Detection Platform (Active Development)
Sentra is a browser extension (Gmail/Outlook) and Flask/PostgreSQL backend that detects phishing emails, built by a 4-person team with Quy serving as Cybersecurity Analyst & Developer. Repo: https://github.com/Phishing-Detection-Team/fraudify

Quy designed a regex pre-flight filter modeled on known jailbreak and prompt-injection patterns (DAN, ChatML tokens, instruction-override phrasing) that blocks attacks before they ever reach the LLM, cutting response time on blocked attempts from a 15-20 second model inference call to under 5 milliseconds. He red-teamed the filter against 41 real attack payloads, found the most common jailbreak phrase slipping through, and patched the gap — lifting the block rate by 10 percentage points with zero false positives on legitimate email.

He also closed a hidden-content injection vector in the browser extension by parsing email bodies with `innerText` rather than `textContent`, keeping CSS-hidden payloads out of the analyzer, and applied NIST CSF data-integrity practices to the PostgreSQL layer: bcrypt password hashing, 20 check constraints, and 15 field validators enforced at both the database and ORM layers across 5 models. This project is Quy's direct technical answer to the phishing attack he suffered as a kid.

An AI-powered operator that autonomously monitors and surfaces the latest cybersecurity threats, news, and trends. Will use external APIs to pull real-time threat intelligence into an LLM-based pipeline, delivering curated updates without manual noise filtering. Tech stack is being finalized.

## CyberLab (Planned)
A self-hosted personal cybersecurity exploration environment for hands-on offensive and defensive security practice, complementing TryHackMe and HackTheBox with a fully controlled lab setup.

## Skills — Overview

Incident Response, Endpoint Security, Vulnerability & Patch Management, Malware Containment, Threat Analysis, NIST CSF, Prompt Injection Defense, OSINT, Network Segmentation. In practice, Quy has responded to real security incidents — identifying and remediating unpatched endpoints and isolating compromised machines from the network. He understands prompt injection attacks and has engineered defenses against them in AI systems. He trains on TryHackMe and HackTheBox across network security, malware analysis, and OSINT (lab/coursework exposure), and follows senior professionals and community discourse to stay current on emerging threats.

## Machine Learning & AI Skills
Quy works across the ML pipeline: data curation and validation, model integration, and translating model output into real findings — including Python/OpenCV video tracking and model evaluation workflows for a zebrafish drug-response research project. He also approaches AI from a security lens — engineering prompt-injection and jailbreak defenses for LLM-facing systems rather than just building models. AI Security skills: Prompt Injection Defense, Jailbreak Red-Teaming, Model Evaluation, Input Validation, OpenCV.

## Programming & Development Skills
Python, SQL, C, C++, Java, JavaScript, HTML/CSS. Quy's strongest language is Python, which he uses across automation, backend APIs, data pipelines, and security tooling. He has built Flask/PostgreSQL applications with bcrypt password hashing and check-constraint/field-validator data integrity enforced at both the database and ORM layers.

Manages enterprise-scale device fleets across Windows and macOS, and is comfortable operating across Windows, Linux, and macOS environments. ## Soft Skills
Detail-Oriented, Problem Solving, Critical Thinking, Communication, Time Management, Customer Service, Teaching & Mentorship. Quy actively educates university staff and students on protecting personal and organizational information online — bridging technical security with human behavior. His background in customer-facing roles has sharpened his ability to explain complex technical issues clearly, build trust quickly, and adapt his communication style to any audience, from engineers to first-time users.
